other.repeated: turning and retreatment for a further 1 h

evidence.quote: To ensure a chemical homogeneity, samples were treated by induction heating at high power (at ∼1573 K) for 1 h, followed by turning and retreatment for a further 1 h.
After homogenization, samples were subsequently hot rolled at 1523 K with reduction in thickness by 20 to 30%
cold rolled with reduction in thickness by 90%
annealed at 1473 K for 10 min
aged at 873 K for 2 h

attributes.composition: enriched in Al, Ta, and Ni

evidence.quote: the aging treatment generates the precipitation of coherent γ′ particles sized at 3 to 7 nm with a high volume fraction (28.2 ± 2.4%) in the fcc matrix
The volume fraction of NiAl after aging was 3.8 ± 0.5%, mainly along grain boundaries.
The diffraction patterns obtained from X-ray diffraction (XRD) show that the initial specimen has a single fcc phase

attributes.description: mixture of equiaxed fine grains and elongated coarse grains

evidence.quote: After thermomechanical processing, a heterogeneous austenite structure was obtained comprising a mixture of equiaxed fine grains and elongated coarse grains in the recrystallized state (Fig. 1a). The average sizes of the fine and coarse grains are 5.4 ± 3.8 μm and 28.4 ± 11.7 μm, respectively
the lattice parameter of the fcc matrix is a 0 = 0.3605 nm
the lattice parameter of the bcc martensite is a = 0.2908 nm
the active strengthening mechanisms at elevated temperatures primarily involved ordered L1 2 gamma prime precipitates
the grain-boundary pinning effect that arises from the thermodynamically stable grain-boundary NiAl phase
the heterogeneous structure composed of ﬁne-grained and coarse-grained domains in FeNiCoAlTaB does not degrade at high temperatures
high-density nanotwins with an ultraﬁne spacing of 6–10 nm
deformation-induced microbands are observed (Fig. 8 c)
The current metastable alloy presents good ductility and superior engineering tensile strengths of 2.2 GPa, 1.4 GPa, 80 0 MPa, and 50 0 MPa at 77 K, 298 K, 873 K, and 1073 K, respectively.

the deformation of the FeNiCoAlTaB alloy at 77 K shows an abnormal resurgence in strain hardening, reaching a strain-hardening rate of ∼18 GPa at a true strain of ∼0.095
The strain recovery ratio ( ε Recov erable / ε F orward ) attains 85% in the 1st cycle and slightly decreases in the subsequent cycles to ∼75% by the 7th cycle.
The pseudoelastic strain shows a fast increase to a steady level at ∼1.8% in the 3rd cycle, accompanied by a resurgence in strain hardening.
The energy dissipation ratio of the FeNiCoAlTaB alloy exceeds ∼9% when the stress levels are ∼1.2 GPa
